title: Two Line-ups and Their Taller-Neighbour Numbers
description: Under the heading "Two Line-ups and Their Taller-Neighbour Numbers", two horizontal panels display eight children of distinct heights standing on blue ground lines. In the top panel, labelled "First line", speech bubbles above the children read from left to right: "0", "2", "1", "1", "0", "2", "1", and "0". In the bottom panel, labelled "After rearranging", the same eight children stand in a different order with bubbles reading from left to right: "1", "0", "2", "0", "1", "2", "1", and "0". A logo and watermark read "SINGULARITY".

title: Three Possible Line-ups of Five Children
description: Three panels show five children standing in line under the title "Three Possible Line-ups of Five Children". Each child has a numbered bubble above them. The left panel shows increasing heights with bubbles "1", "1", "1", "1", "0", labeled "Shortest to tallest" and "1, 1, 1, 1, 0". The middle panel shows heights "150 cm", "140 cm", "120 cm", "135 cm", "145 cm" with bubbles "0", "1", "2", "1", "0" and "0, 1, 2, 1, 0". The right panel shows heights "150 cm", "120 cm", "145 cm", "125 cm", "140 cm" with bubbles "0", "2", "0", "2", "0" and "0, 2, 0, 2, 0". A yellow star marks the tallest child saying "0" in each panel. Banners below read "The tallest child says 0" and "End children never say 2".

title: Shaded Cells Beat Their Neighbours
labels: Supercell: larger than all its neighbours
description: A title banner reads 'Shaded Cells Beat Their Neighbours'. Below sit two rows of eight rounded rectangular cells. The top row contains '43', '79', '75', '63', '10', '29', '28', and '34', where '79', '29', and '34' are shaded peach with orange borders while the others have blue borders. The bottom row displays '200', '577', '626', '345', '790', '694', '109', and '198', with '626', '790', and '198' shaded peach. Orange arrows point up to two shaded cells: one labelled 'Larger than 577 and 345' points to '626', and another labelled 'Only one neighbour, 109' points to '198'. A bottom blue pill reads 'Supercell: larger than all its neighbours'.

title: Alternate to Get the Most Supercells
labels: Most supercells: half the cells, rounded up
description: Under the heading 'Alternate to Get the Most Supercells', a row of nine cells contains '110', '100', '150', '130', '280', '200', '230', '210', and '270'. Five alternating cells are shaded orange, labelled '9 cells: 5 supercells'. Below sit six rows of two, three, four, five, six, and seven empty cells alternating orange and white, beginning with orange. Labels beside them read '2 cells: 1', '3 cells: 2', '4 cells: 2', '5 cells: 3', '6 cells: 3', and '7 cells: 4'. At the bottom, a pill reads 'Most supercells: half the cells, rounded up', beside branding for 'SINGULARITY'.

title: Supercells in a Grid Beat Four Neighbours
labels: A supercell beats its left, right, top and bottom neighbours
description: A top banner reads "Supercells in a Grid Beat Four Neighbours". Below on the left, labelled "Table 1: 8632 and its four neighbours", five cells form a cross with orange-shaded "8632" pointing outward to "4795", "1944", "4580" and "8280". On the right, under "Table 2: completed", sits a four-by-four grid of sixteen five-digit numbers. Five cells are shaded orange: "96,310", "39,160", "60,319", "10,963", and "69,031". Eleven other cells have blue borders: "96,301", "36,109", "96,103", "13,609", "19,306", "13,906", "10,396", "60,193", "60,931", "10,369", and "10,936". A bottom banner states "A supercell beats its left, right, top and bottom neighbours".

topic_name: Patterns of Numbers on the Number Line
title: Eleven Numbers on a Line from 1000 to 10,000
description: A horizontal dark blue number line has ten equally spaced ticks labeled '1000', '2000', '3000', '4000', '5000', '6000', '7000', '8000', '9000', and '10,000' below the line. A blue caption at the bottom reads 'One tick for every thousand'. Above the line, eleven orange arrows drop from staggered rounded labels to their scaled locations: '1050', '1500', '2180', '2754', '3050', '3600', '5030', '5300', '8400', '9590', and '9950'. A title banner at the top reads 'Eleven Numbers on a Line from 1000 to 10,000'.

topic_name: Patterns of Numbers on the Number Line
title: Step = Difference ÷ Gaps on Line a
description: A horizontal number line displays ten equally spaced ticks labelled from left to right: "1990", "1995", "2000", "2005", "2010", "2015", "2020", "2025", "2030", and "2035". The leftmost label "1990" is circled in purple, and the rightmost label "2035" is enclosed in a purple box. The fifth label "2010" and seventh label "2020" are highlighted in orange rounded outlines. An orange bracket labelled "2 gaps" spans two orange hop arrows between 2010 and 2020. Stacked to the right are "2020 - 2010 = 10", "10 ÷ 2 = 5", and a green badge "Step: 5". A top banner reads "Step = Difference ÷ Gaps on Line a".

title: Choices in Each Place Give 9, 90, 900, 9000, 90,000
description: A diagram titled "Choices in Each Place Give 9, 90, 900, 9000, 90,000" displays five horizontal rows labeled "1-digit", "2-digit", "3-digit", "4-digit", and "5-digit". An orange badge at the top reads "First place: never 0" with an arrow pointing down. Each row contains square boxes representing digit positions: one box in row 1 up to five boxes in row 5. The first box in every row is orange containing "9" with "1 to 9" underneath. Subsequent boxes are blue-bordered containing "10" with "0 to 9" underneath. To the right of each row are the corresponding products: "9", "9 × 10 = 90", "9 × 10 × 10 = 900", "9 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 9000", and "9 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 90,000".

title: Counting the Digit 7 Place by Place
description: A title banner at the top reads "Counting the Digit 7 Place by Place". Below are two main panels. The left panel is headed "1 to 100" with two columns: "Ones place" lists "7", "17", "27", three vertical dots, an orange-boxed "77", three vertical dots, and "97", above "10 times"; "Tens place" lists "70", three vertical dots, an orange-boxed "77", three vertical dots, and "79", above "10 times". An orange double-headed arrow connects both "77" boxes, labeled "77 has two 7s". Below sits "10 + 10 = 20". The right panel is headed "1 to 1000" with three columns labeled "Hundreds", "Tens", and "Ones", each ending in "100 times". The hundreds column also shows "700 to 799". Below sits "100 + 100 + 100 = 300".

title: Same Digit Sum 14, Very Different Sizes
labels: more zeros in the middle: bigger number, same digit sum
description: A heading banner reads "Same Digit Sum 14, Very Different Sizes" above five light blue columns labeled "ten-thousands", "thousands", "hundreds", "tens", and "ones". Three right-aligned rows of blue-bordered digit boxes display numbers. The first row has boxes "5" and "9", tagged "smallest: 59" and "digit sum 14". The second row has "9", "5", "0", "0", "0", tagged "largest 5-digit: 95,000" and "digit sum 14". The third row has "9", "0", "0", "5", tagged "9005" and "digit sum 14". An orange arrow at the bottom points to "more zeros in the middle: bigger number, same digit sum".

title: Consecutive Digits Even Out to Three Middles
description: A title reads "Consecutive Digits Even Out to Three Middles". Below, two side-by-side panels show towers of unit squares. In the left panel, under a badge reading "345", three columns contain 3, 4, and 5 squares labeled "3", "4", and "5". The top square of the 5-column is orange, and an orange arrow curves from it to an orange dashed outline above the 3-column. Below sit "3 + 4 + 5 = 12" and "one less, middle, one more". In the right panel, three columns each contain 4 blue-outlined squares, labeled "4", "4", and "4". Below sit "3 × 4 = 12" and "three middles".

title: All Nine 3-Digit Palindromes from 1, 2 and 3
description: A grid of nine white rounded cards is arranged in three rows and three columns below the heading "All Nine 3-Digit Palindromes from 1, 2 and 3". Row labels on the left read "ends 1", "ends 2", and "ends 3". Column labels along the top read "middle 1", "middle 2", and "middle 3". The first row contains "111", "121", and "131". The second row contains "212", "222", and "232". The third row contains "313", "323", and "333". Each palindrome has blue matching outer digits joined by an arched blue line, with an orange middle digit. Below the grid, a green-bordered pill displays "3 × 3 = 9".

title: Reverse and Add: Four Starts, Four Palindromes
description: A heading banner reads 'Reverse and Add: Four Starts, Four Palindromes' above four light-blue vertical panels. Each panel presents vertical addition with right-aligned digits. The first panel shows '34' over '+ 43', yielding a green-outlined '77' labelled 'palindrome' and '1 round' below. The second shows '29' over '+ 92', giving green-outlined '121' labelled 'palindrome' and '1 round'. The third shows '48' over '+ 84', giving '132' labelled 'not a palindrome', then '+ 231' giving green-outlined '363' labelled 'palindrome' and '2 rounds'. The fourth shows '76' over '+ 67', giving '143' labelled 'not a palindrome', then '+ 341' giving green-outlined '484' labelled 'palindrome' and '2 rounds'.

title: From 10:01 to 12:21: Two Gaps of 70 Minutes
description: A horizontal timeline shows four ticks labelled in rounded badges: '10:01', '11:01', '11:11', and '12:21'. Dashed vertical lines connect the ticks at '10:01', '11:11', and '12:21' to dark clock displays showing those times in green, each topped with the label 'palindromic time'. Above the line, blue arcs jump from '10:01' to '11:01' labelled '60 min', '11:01' to '11:11' labelled '10 min', and '11:11' to '12:21' labelled '70 min'. An orange bracket over the first two intervals is labelled '70 min'. Below the line, a wide bracket spans from '10:01' to '12:21' with a box reading '70 + 70 = 140 minutes'.

title: Checking a Palindromic Date by Reversing Eight Digits
description: Under the heading "Checking a Palindromic Date by Reversing Eight Digits", two stacked panels compare date digits. The top panel shows "10/02/2001" with eight blue boxes labeled "digits" reading 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0, 1 and eight matching green boxes labeled "reversed" reading 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0, 1 beside "same: palindromic date". The bottom panel shows "01/02/2001" with "digits" row 0, 1, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0, 1 and "reversed" row 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, 0, 1, 0. Positions 1, 2, 7, and 8 have red dotted lines and red boxes with crosses beside "not the same".

title: Weekday Shifts from 2025 to 2031 Make a Whole Week
description: A heading banner reads "Weekday Shifts from 2025 to 2031 Make a Whole Week". Below, seven rounded cards are arranged horizontally: green "2025", blue "2026", blue "2027", orange "2028", blue "2029", blue "2030", and green "2031". Above "2028" is an orange badge reading "leap year". Five blue arrows labelled "+1" connect the ordinary years, while an orange arrow labelled "+2" connects "2028" to "2029". Blue badges underneath track running sums: "total 1", "total 2", "total 3", "total 5", and "total 6", ending with green badges "total 7" and "a whole week" under "2031". A green bracket labelled "same calendar" links "2025" and "2031".

title: Kaprekar's Loop: 6382 Runs to 6174
labels: Largest number from the digits: A
Smallest number from the digits: B
description: Under the heading "Kaprekar's Loop: 6382 Runs to 6174", a flowchart on the left contains four boxes linked by downward arrows: "Take a 4-digit number", "Largest number from the digits: A", "Smallest number from the digits: B", and "C = A - B", with an orange return arrow labeled "use the digits of C". To the right, below "start: 6382", four sequential cards show rounds of subtraction: "round 1" with "A = 8632", "B = 2368", "C = 6264"; "round 2" with "A = 6642", "B = 2466", "C = 4176"; "round 3" with "A = 7641", "B = 1467", "C = 6174"; and "round 4" repeating "A = 7641", "B = 1467", "C = 6174". A green bracket tags rounds 3 and 4 as "stuck at 6174".

title: Keep Four Digits: the Smallest from 8, 5, 5, 0 Is 0558
description: Under a header reading "Keep Four Digits: the Smallest from 8, 5, 5, 0 Is 0558", three blue panels sit side by side. The left panel contains four loose tiles with digits "8", "5", "5", and "0". The middle panel shows a top row of four tiles reading "8", "5", "5", "0" next to "A = 8550", and a bottom row reading "0", "5", "5", "8" next to "B = 0558", with the initial "0" highlighted in orange. Underneath are the boxed equation "8550 - 0558 = 7992" and "0558 is 558". The right panel displays "999 → 0999" with an orange-highlighted leading "0", captioned "always keep four digits".

title: Middle Numbers Joined by Arrows to 38,800 and 3400
description: A title banner at the top reads "Middle Numbers Joined by Arrows to 38,800 and 3400". Thirteen rounded number boxes are arranged in three columns. The middle column has five blue boxes with "25,000", "400", "13,000", "1500", and "60,000". The left column has an orange box with "38,800", followed by blue boxes with "28,000", "61,600", and "31,000". The right column has a purple box with "3400", followed by blue boxes with "63,000", "19,500", and "20,900". Four orange arrows lead to "38,800": one from "25,000", two from "400", and one from "13,000". Three purple arrows lead to "3400": one from "400" and two from "1500".

title: Hops of 400 Jump Over 1000
description: A horizontal dark blue number line displays five marked values from left to right: "0", "400", "800", "1000", and "1200". Blue dots mark the ticks at "0", "400", "800", and "1200". Three equal curved blue hops, each labelled "+ 400" inside a blue badge, arc from 0 to 400, 400 to 800, and 800 to 1200. Centred above the hops is a badge reading "Counting in 400s". The tick at 1000 sits halfway between 800 and 1200 inside an open red circle, with a red-bordered box below reading "Skipped". At the top, a heading reads "Hops of 400 Jump Over 1000".

title: Six Number Boxes and Four Targets to Build
description: Under the heading "Six Number Boxes and Four Targets to Build", a light blue panel on the left displays six rounded boxes under a tag reading "Add or subtract". The boxes hold "40,000", "7000", "300", "1500", "12,000", and "800". On the right, five horizontal boxes present targets. The top box, with a green border, shows the worked example "39,800 = 40,000 - 800 + 300 + 300". The remaining four boxes, outlined in blue, display "45,000 = ?", "5900 = ?", "17,500 = ?", and "21,400 = ?".

topic_name: How Many Digits? Sums and Differences
title: Where 5-Digit Sums and Differences Can Land
description: Heading at top reads "Where 5-Digit Sums and Differences Can Land". Two horizontal panels each show a number line. The top panel, titled "Sum of two 5-digit numbers", features a light green band bounded by ticks at "20,000" and "1,99,998", with boxed calculations "10,000 + 10,000 = 20,000" and "99,999 + 99,999 = 1,99,998" below them. To the left, a crossed red circle marks "18,500" labelled "Impossible". The bottom panel, titled "Difference of two 5-digit numbers", has a green band from "0" to "89,999" with "99,999 - 10,000 = 89,999" below the right tick. To the right, a crossed red circle marks "91,500" labelled "Impossible".

topic_name: How Many Digits? Sums and Differences
title: 4-Digit Plus 2-Digit Sums Against the Digit Zones
description: A horizontal strip is divided into three equal rectangular zones labeled "4 digits" in blue, "5 digits" in yellow, and "6 digits" in purple, separated by boundary ticks at "10,000" and "1,00,000". A pill label reads "4-digit number + 2-digit number". Below, an orange horizontal bar spans from inside "4 digits" to just past "10,000" into "5 digits", with dashed lines linking to end labels "1000 + 10 = 1010" and "9999 + 99 = 10,098". A red-outlined label inside "6 digits" reads "Gives 6 digits: never", and an orange box below reads "Gives 4 digits: only sometimes". A header reads "4-Digit Plus 2-Digit Sums Against the Digit Zones", with watermark text "SINGULARITY".

title: Three Number Patterns to Total: Rows, Dice and a Grid
description: Under a banner titled 'Three Number Patterns to Total: Rows, Dice and a Grid' with a 'SINGULARITY' logo, three panels labeled 'a', 'b', and 'c' present numerical patterns. Panel 'a' contains five interlocking rows: twelve orange cards showing '40' across three rows and ten blue cards showing '50' across two rows. Panel 'b' shows an 8 by 8 grid of 64 dice faces: 20 purple faces with five white pips forming five 2 by 2 blocks, and 44 teal faces with one white pip. Panel 'c' shows an arch-shaped grid with 32 blue cells showing '32' across four full rows, above 16 orange cells showing '64'.

title: A Dice Grid with Matching Rows and Circles in Rings
description: Under the heading "A Dice Grid with Matching Rows and Circles in Rings", two panels are labeled "d" and "f", with a corner logo marked "SINGULARITY". Panel "d" shows a 7 by 5 grid of dice: rows 1 through 5 and row 7 each show 3, 4, 4, 4, and 3 pips, with the middle twelve four-pip faces of rows 2 to 5 highlighted in red and the rest in teal. Row 6 shows five teal faces of 3 pips. Panel "f" has concentric rings around a central circle showing "1000": 4 circles showing "500", 8 showing "250", and 18 showing "125".

title: A Hexagon of 15s, 25s and 35s
description: A large hexagon contains seven yellow hexagonal pieces and six blue corner pieces, marked with letter "e" at upper left. Above, a banner reads "A Hexagon of 15s, 25s and 35s" with a "SINGULARITY" logo. Blue corner pieces each display four numbers: "15" at top left and bottom right, "25" at top right and bottom left, and "35" at left and right. Outer yellow hexagons contain six numbers each: "35" above and below center, "25" at upper left and lower right, and "15" at upper right and lower left. The center hexagon contains two each of "15", "25", and "35" across a "SINGULARITY" watermark.

topic_name: An Unsolved Mystery: the Collatz Conjecture
title: Powers of 2 Halve Straight Down to 1
description: Seven bars stand along a horizontal baseline, decreasing in height from left to right: '64', '32', '16', '8', '4', '2', and '1'. The first six bars are pale blue with blue borders, each half the height of the bar to its left, while the last bar is an orange outline stub. Below the baseline, blue pill tags read 'even' under each of the first six bars, and an orange tag reads 'end' under '1'. Six curved orange arrows link the numbers, each labelled 'half'. At the top, a banner reads 'Powers of 2 Halve Straight Down to 1'.

title: Paromita's Estimate: One Class, Then Five
description: A chart titled "Paromita's Estimate: One Class, Then Five" displays five columns labelled "Class 6", "Class 7", "Class 8", "Class 9", and "Class 10". Above "Class 6", orange text reads "Paromita's class". Class 6 contains three solid blue boxes stacked vertically with numbers "32", "29", and "35". Above Classes 7 to 10, a bracket is labelled "assumed similar", and each of these four columns contains three empty dashed blue boxes. Beneath each of the five columns sits an oval labelled "about 100". To the right, a blue box reads "5 × 100 = 500", with a blue downward arrow pointing to a green box reading "About 500 students".

title: Working Back from 21: The Safe Numbers
description: A heading banner reads "Working Back from 21: The Safe Numbers". A horizontal row displays 21 squares. The 1st, 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, and 21st squares are shaded light orange, bordered in orange, and contain the numbers "1", "5", "9", "13", "17", and "21". The other 15 squares are white with blue borders, appearing in groups of three. Above the track, five curved orange arrows jump backward from right to left, each labelled "4 back". An orange box above square 21 is labelled "Target" with a downward arrow. At the lower left, an orange square sits beside "Safe". A faint central watermark reads "SINGULARITY".

title: Who Wins? The First Move and the First Safe Number
labels: First player reaches 2: first player wins
First move cannot reach 11: second player wins
description: Two panels appear under the title "Who Wins? The First Move and the First Safe Number". The top panel, "Race to 22: add 1, 2 or 3", shows 23 squares, highlighting safe numbers "2", "6", "10", "14", "18", and "22". An arrow jumps from "0" to "2", a bracket marks "first move: 1, 2 or 3", and a tag reads "First player reaches 2: first player wins". The bottom panel, "Race to 99: add 1 to 10", shows a line ticked by elevens from "0" to "99". A marker for "first move: 1 to 10" stops before "11", captioned "First move cannot reach 11: second player wins".
